newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: ALPINE SKIING-WIBERG LEADS AFTER FIRST LEG OF SLALOM.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-WIBERG LEADS AFTER FIRST LEG OF SLALOM.

text.p: Sweden's Pernilla Wiberg took advantage of an early start number to snatch the lead in the first leg of a women's World Cup slalom on Saturday.
The first skier onto the icy Nationale course, Wiberg, the slalom world champion, clocked a time of 44.60 seconds.
New Zealand's Claudia Riegler, winner of the season opening slalom in Park City, followed the Swede out of the start hut and was the only other skier to go under 45 seconds, crossing in 44.83.
World championship silver medallist Patricia Chauvet of France was third in 45.24 with Switzerland's Karin Roten fourth in 45.41.

Austria's Elfi Eder, last season's overall slalom champion, and Deborah Compagnoni of Italy, the Olympic and world giant slalom champion, both crashed out on the tricky layout that claimed 10 of the first 30 skiers.
Germany's Katja Seizinger, the overall World Cup leader, was suffering from the flu did not race.
